scenes.caption: Bad loans fell from 11.5% to 2.8%. What that number hides.
scenes.narration: India's bank bad loans have fallen sharply. But what does that number leave out?

scenes.title: Gross bad loans, all scheduled banks (RBI data via PIB)
scenes.caption: Peak in 2018. Down to 2.79% by 2025.
scenes.narration: Bad loans were four point one percent of all bank lending in twenty fourteen, peaked at eleven and a half percent in twenty eighteen, and were down to two point eight in twenty twenty five.

scenes.kicker: Part of the rise was recognition
scenes.caption: The Finance Ministry says 2018 mostly showed stress being counted honestly.
scenes.narration: The Finance Ministry says much of that rise was stress being counted honestly after a twenty fifteen review, not new trouble.

scenes.kicker: Public sector banks, written off in about 5½ years
scenes.label: about 2.25 times the bad loans left across all banks
scenes.note: Rough comparison. A write-off is not a waiver.
scenes.narration: And public sector banks wrote off six point one six lakh crore rupees. A write-off removes a loan from the count, but the debt is not forgiven.

scenes.caption: What did recapitalising the banks cost the public? No source we read says.
scenes.narration: What we could not find is what the clean-up cost the public.
